Simultaneous critical values

Source: R/effect-inference.R
simultaneous_critical_value.Rd

Returns the multiplier c such that the interval estimate plus or minus c standard errors covers every coordinate of a group jointly with probability level: the level quantile of the largest absolute standardized deviation within the group. This is the max-modulus value that effect_inference() uses for its simultaneous intervals.

Usage

simultaneous_critical_value(
  covariance = NULL,
  draws = NULL,
  estimate = NULL,
  groups = NULL,
  level = 0.95,
  simulations = 10000L,
  seed = NULL
)

Arguments

covariance

A covariance matrix of the coordinates.

draws

A matrix with one row per coordinate and one column per posterior draw.

estimate

The point estimate of each row of draws.

groups

Optional group of each coordinate. Each group gets its own critical value; a covariance is then split into its diagonal blocks.

level

Joint coverage probability.

simulations

Number of Gaussian draws for a covariance.

seed

Optional seed for those draws. The previous random state is restored, so a seed makes the value reproducible without disturbing the caller's random stream.

Value

A numeric vector with the critical value of each coordinate's group, one element per coordinate.

Details

Give either covariance, for a Gaussian vector with that covariance, or draws and estimate, for posterior draws. A covariance gives a value estimated from simulations Gaussian draws and is never below the pointwise normal quantile. Draws are standardized by each row's draw standard deviation. Coordinates with no variance are ignored.

See also

effect_inference()
